target_customer: Manufacturers and digital health companies selling at-home rapid diagnostic tests
problem: Users misread lateral flow tests and companies cannot capture results reliably. Scanbase turns a photo of a rapid test into a result through an API.
business_model: Usage-based API, with later services for integration and support per the company site
product_category: Computer vision API for diagnostic tests

founders.name: Jeffrey Lange
founders.background_notes: YC page does not list prior employers.

founders.name: Steve Roger
founders.background_notes: 10+ years building enterprise APIs per YC page.

competitors.name: TiraSpot (Spotlab)
competitors.what: Smartphone AI platform for reading and reporting rapid diagnostic tests, published as a study
competitors.traction_then: Field tested on antibody tests in a study

technical_complexity.rationale: Reading varied test brands under different lighting needs a trained vision model and per brand validation, with regulatory expectations for medical use.

defensibility.rationale: A dataset of labeled test images could compound, but test makers can build in house or use similar vision tools, and COVID demand fell after 2022.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows an incumbent copying or buying Scanbase. A directory notes no public news after August 2023.

market_need_then: COVID rapid tests surged in 2020 to 2022 and academic work in 2022 studied AI apps for reading lateral flow results, showing demand for objective readings. Demand for COVID tests then declined.

identity.voice_and_tone: Plain and technical, describing solutions for digital health diagnostics

brand_strength.rationale: No brand press or community found. The name overlaps with older unrelated SCANBASE trademark filings and many scanning products.

outcome_analysis: Scanbase launched in the Winter 2023 batch with an API for reading photos of rapid tests, near the end of the COVID testing surge. Its own site now emphasizes consulting, integration and support alongside the API, which may signal a shift, but no source states one. A directory reports no further funding or trade news after August 2023. The record is too thin to assign clear success or failure factors.
notes: Funding unverified. Aggregators report $500K (CB Insights, April 2023, Liquid 2 Ventures), $2.5M seed (Signalbase), $2M (Extruct) and $5M (PitchBook). A directory cites an SEC Form D from May 2023 for a vehicle named Scanbase Leonis raising $321,426 from 110 investors, not verified against the filing. YC page says seed stage. Recurring investors in aggregators: Y Combinator, TRAC, Liquid 2 Ventures, Rebel Fund, Lobster Capital. HQ Los Angeles per YC data, San Francisco in the YC description. Only one dated competitor found.
